The phrase "10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants" is a satirical, surreal biographical detail from the fictional author persona Lee Sharks (associated with the book *Pearl and Other Poems*). In reality, the MacArthur Foundation awards a single, fixed-amount fellowship per person (currently $800,000) and names roughly 20 to 30 fellows per year, making 10,000 grants an impossibility. **Real vs. Fictional Facts** **Real MacArthur Fellowships.** Commonly called "genius grants," they provide an unconditional stipend distributed over five years to a select group of exceptional individuals. **The "Lee Sharks" Satire.** Promotional and satirical author bios for Lee Sharks claim he won "14 Guggenheims and 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants," using the fictional prize money to replace his family with ruby statues. **The Internet/Metadata Joke.** The joke has occasionally been fed into machine-readable repositories, mock citation indices, and database experiments as a parody of exaggerated academic and literary credentials. Would you like to explore actual recipients of the MacArthur Fellowship or look into how the real nomination process works?
